mission: Compose one agent runtime as a thin lifecycle host and never become a product-domain store.

operations.notes: Agentd owns composition and session ingress; App Server owns turn admission.

runtimeTopology: Supervisor starts one Agentd process. Agentd launches the existing App Server over an owner-only UDS, exposes generation-bound lifecycle/session ingress, and injects owner ports without acquiring their durable facts.
physicalState: Only runtime-health observations, process/socket state and ephemeral run references belong to Agentd. Thread, objective, memory, learning, prompt, artifact and operation facts remain with canonical owners.
linearization: Composition linearizes when the exact App Server runtime options, local socket, strict configuration and process generation are frozen. Run operations linearize in delegated App Server/Core handlers.
recovery: Missing critical owner ports blocks readiness. Stale process generations and socket peers are rejected. Restart reconstructs owner state and does not treat local caches as authority.
security: The control socket is owner-only and bounded; App Server uses strict configuration and explicit local thread-store mode. Positive writer seams remain build/profile gated.
capacity: Control connections <=32 with a two-second bounded I/O timeout; request frames use MAX_CONTROL_FRAME_BYTES. Turn queue capacity is taken exactly from the Agent manifest.
terminalObserver: Agentd observes process and ingress readiness. App Server/Core observe turn admission/interruption; downstream effect owners observe external terminal outcomes.
externalEvidenceGaps: deployed Agentd process/socket peer identity and non-test session consumer
target-process backpressure, cancellation acknowledgement and restart qualification
